(a) Maximum Under SGLI.—Section 1967 of title 38, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a)(3)(A)(i), by striking “$250,000” and inserting “$400,000”; and  
        (2) in subsection (d), by striking “of $250,000” and inserting “in effect under paragraph (3)(A)(i) of that subsection”.   
    (b) Maximum Under VGLI.—Section 1977(a) of such title is amended—
        (1) in paragraph (1), by striking “in excess of $250,000 at any one time” and inserting “at any one time in excess of the maximum amount for Servicemembers’ Group Life Insurance in effect under section 1967(a)(3)(A)(i) of this title”; and  
        (2) in paragraph (2)—
            (A) by striking “for less than $250,000 under Servicemembers’ Group Life Insurance” and inserting “under Servicemembers’ Group Life Insurance for less than the maximum amount for such insurance in effect under section 1967(a)(3)(A)(i) of this title”; and  
            (B) by striking “does not exceed $250,000” and inserting “does not exceed such maximum amount in effect under such section”.    
    (c) Effective Date.—The amendments made by this section shall take effect as of September 1, 2005, and shall apply with respect to deaths occurring on or after that date.

fable.w: This section only raises the maximum coverage amounts for Servicemembers' and Veterans' Group Life Insurance and sets an effective date. No tempting reading exists: there is no consultation, comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.

opus.w: The section only raises the maximum SGLI and VGLI coverage amounts and sets an effective date. It has no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking authority, advisory body, or right to sue. A section about insurance benefits does not on its own involve outside parties in a federal decision.
opus.b: Step 1: The only tempting reading is that insurance or benefit amounts involve the public. That fails because the section just changes dollar caps and sets an effective date. No outside party takes part in any federal decision, and benefit amounts and applications don't count as participation anyway.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends statutory text to increase insurance coverage limits and update cross-references. It does not require or recommend any consultation, public comment, hearing, or coordination with outside parties (such as veterans or the general public) before the decision to change the limits is made. The actors involved are Congress amending the law and the Secretary administering it, which are internal government actions.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Maximum Under SGLI.—Section 1967 of title 38, United States Code, is amended— (1) in subsection (a)(3)(A)(i), by striking “$250,000” and inserting “$400,000”; and (2) in subsection (d), by striking “of $250,000” and inserting “in effect under paragraph (3)(A)(i) of that subsection”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing insurance limits affects veterans or servicemembers (outsiders), so it involves them. However, the text itself only describes statutory amendments to dollar amounts and effective dates. It does not describe any process of consulting, hearing from, or coordinating with those individuals. The definition requires an interaction *before* a decision, not just the existence of a rule that affects outsiders.
